rounds.name: Recruiter Screen
rounds.focus: Background, motivation, basic fit. India note: Amazon India (Hyderabad/Bangalore) hires heavily for PM-T roles from IIMs/IITs and top engineering schools; the loop mirrors the global process but is almost always fully virtual, and interviewers/Bar Raiser may dial in from other geographies.
questions: Tell me about yourself
Why do you want to work at Amazon?
How would you define the role of a product manager?
What product that you led are you most proud of, and why?
Walk me through your background and what you're working on now

rounds.name: Leadership Principles / Behavioral
rounds.format: 60 min 1:1 onsite interview, ~2-3 Leadership Principles per interviewer
rounds.focus: Deep behavioral stories mapped to Amazon's 16 Leadership Principles
rounds.evaluates: Customer Obsession, Ownership, Bias for Action, Earn Trust, Dive Deep, Deliver Results
questions: Tell me about a time you disagreed with a decision and had to commit anyway (Have Backbone; Disagree and Commit)
Describe a time you dug into data that contradicted the prevailing anecdote (Dive Deep)
Tell me about a customer-first decision you made under business pressure (Customer Obsession)
Tell me about a time you aligned conflicting stakeholders around one plan (Earn Trust)
Describe how you negotiated priorities without formal authority (Ownership)
Tell me about a time you used AI to drive innovation or simplify a process (Invent and Simplify)
Tell me about a time you sacrificed short-term results for long-term strategy (Think Big)
Give an example of building trust with a skeptical partner team

rounds.name: Functional Product Skills
rounds.format: 60 min 1:1 onsite interview with a PM/PM-T
rounds.focus: Product sense, roadmap ownership, prioritization case
questions: Tell me about a time you influenced a product roadmap
How do you decide what to build when requirements conflict?
Walk me through how you set and defended a product vision
Improve or design a product in your domain (live product sense case)
How would you prioritize a backlog with three equally-loud stakeholders?
Design a feature to increase Prime adoption among first-time Amazon India shoppers

rounds.name: Technical Depth (PM-T specific)
rounds.format: 60 min 1:1 onsite interview, sometimes includes a system-design component
rounds.focus: Technical/architectural fluency for Product Manager - Technical candidates
rounds.evaluates: Technical judgment, systems thinking, ability to partner credibly with engineers
questions: What core technologies power your product domain?
How did you identify gaps or opportunities across features or system architectures?
Share an example where you used data and technical judgment to drive a decision
Describe the high-level system components of a product like YouTube or LinkedIn
Walk me through how you'd design a recommendation system for a retail product page
How technical do your PM-T stories need to be - describe a time you pushed back on an engineering approach

rounds.name: Bar Raiser
rounds.format: 60 min 1:1 onsite interview with a trained interviewer from outside the hiring org (holds veto power)
rounds.focus: Long-term culture and leadership fit independent of team-level bias
rounds.evaluates: Leadership Principles fit, long-term potential, culture add
questions: Tell me about a time you weren't able to deliver on a commitment
Tell me about a decision you'd revisit, and how you'd approach it differently now
Walk me through a time you took responsibility for a team failure
Which Leadership Principle do you personally struggle with the most?
Tell me about a time you raised the bar on a team that was comfortable with the status quo

rounds.name: Recruiter Screening
rounds.focus: Background verification, role/level fit, motivation. India note: Amazon India TPM hiring is centered in Hyderabad and Bangalore; process and structure mirror the global loop, fully virtual, with Bar Raiser sometimes dialing in from the US or EU.
questions: Tell me about your background and current scope as a TPM
Why Amazon, and why this team?
What's the most complex technical program you've managed?
Walk me through your experience with distributed/technical teams

rounds.name: Program Management Round
rounds.format: 60 min 1:1 onsite interview (5-min intro, 50-min interview, 5-min Q&A)
rounds.focus: Cross-team dependency management, scheduling, stakeholder communication
questions: Describe a program with dependencies across 3+ teams - how did you manage it?
Tell me about a time a program was at risk of missing a deadline - what did you do?
How do you communicate program status to senior leadership?
Walk me through how you'd build a program plan for a launch with unclear requirements
Describe a time you had to descope a program to hit a critical date
How do you decide which risks to escalate versus own yourself?

rounds.name: Technical / System Design
rounds.format: 60 min 1:1 onsite interview with an SDE, SDM, or PM-T
rounds.focus: System design and architecture reasoning appropriate to a technical program
rounds.evaluates: Technical depth, systems thinking, architecture fluency
questions: Design a high-level system for a service that must scale to millions of requests per day
How would you evaluate two competing technical approaches for the same program?
Walk me through a technical trade-off you influenced without being the subject-matter expert
Explain a complex technical concept from a recent program to a non-technical stakeholder
What technical red flags would make you delay a launch?

rounds.name: Leadership Principles / Behavioral
rounds.format: 60 min 1:1 onsite interview, each interviewer assigned specific principles
rounds.focus: Deep behavioral stories across Amazon's 16 Leadership Principles
rounds.evaluates: Customer Obsession, Ownership, Invent and Simplify, Dive Deep, Deliver Results, Bias for Action
questions: Tell me about declining a customer requirement and why
Describe your most innovative project and the challenges you faced
Describe a decision made with incomplete information
Share a recently learned skill and how you learned it
Discuss a time you raised the bar on a successful initiative unprompted
Describe a bold, difficult decision you pushed through despite opposition
Discuss a personal mistake and how you managed the fallout
Describe your proudest accomplishment and what made it hard

rounds.name: Bar Raiser
rounds.format: 60 min 1:1 onsite interview with a cross-org trained interviewer (veto power)
rounds.focus: Long-term leadership potential and culture fit independent of the hiring team
questions: Tell me about a time you disagreed with your manager on something important
Which Leadership Principles resonate most and least with you, and why?
Tell me about a time you tackled a challenge outside your role's scope
Describe a time you persisted on a program when teammates wanted to abandon it
Walk me through a time your program failed - what would you do differently?
